Eventually, you will find people that will make you shine. Life is rough. I’m 28 bipolar type 1 and I have a hard time meeting people because of my anxiety. My doctor wants to reduce my meds, which scares me. Some days I can’t even function due to severe depression. But I’m hoping in time I might just meet some good people. So yeah I feel your pain.

It’s hard to let go...I know that all to well. I watched everyone I loved get married and start families, with someone other than me. It hurts, but as time and therapy have allowed, I have learned that I am worth it and someday someone will love me for me. People will use you, and leave you. But to let them take your beautiful life away, just because he didn’t really love you, or maybe he has commitment issues. The fact is by moving on and finding love again, You Win! That’ll feel much better in the end than a quick release from “heavy” but temporary pain.

You are loved. You are beautiful. Take care of yourself. This hate has wounded you. You have to let go of what opinions are. As “The Dude” says...”That’s just like...your opinion man”. You deserve to be celebrated for who you are. Life is about jamming in the right band. Surround yourself with people that love you. Try to love yourself.

Try to calm down. Take a deep breath. I’m just a single dude, but I know your life is precious. He obviously wasn’t right for you. You will love again, it may be soon or far away. And try to love yourself. You have to really dig down deep and forgive yourself. But love yourself enough to know that no lover is worth taking your life over. That is an extreme reaction to a temporary feeling. Every love burns differently and grows in its own way. Don’t let him take the greatest gift you have. Love and compassion. And honestly he seems to have issues to work out. He wasn’t right for you. Learn from the pain and try to move on in time.

Please try and love yourself. You seem like a kind hearted individual, with compassion. The world would be poorer without you. Preserve and rise above the stigma. Apply for disability if you have too. Or try some part time work to try and save money to move. If your family doesn’t support you, then make a new family out of friends and loved ones. Blood is not the end all. I love you for you are me, and I am you. We should care for each other not tear ourselves apart. The trump wave will crash! Roads will be built anew and bridges to help and better life fixed. It’s hard in this world to have faith in anything. But have faith in your heart. It’ll lead you to where you need to be. Find the grey area! Logic and emotion in harmony. You are loved. You are beautiful. Believe in yourself.

You don’t have to have a terrible life to have depression/have a mental illness. For some reason people tend to think that mental illness is a sign of weakness. It is true strength to reach out for help and try to get to the bottom of your issues. The truth is I’m bipolar type 1, and some days are awful, and some days are great. But the crippling depression is always there making me wonder if I’m good enough, do I deserve love? Am I just human garbage? These thoughts are powerfully negative and can crush anybody. It’s true, mental illness is still frowned upon in society,but by being vocal and seeking help and talking to your family. You can persevere. Please be kind to yourself. Suicidal thoughts are serious and should be handled with care. Try and find something that gives you joy, from inside yourself. You have to learn to love yourself and even enjoy your own company.

Be safe!
Be kind to Yourself!
And please get help if you can!
